description:
Castello di Spessa has a defensive core dating to the 13th century, but its present appearance — crenellated towers, ogival windows — comes from a Neo-Gothic restoration completed between the late 19th and early 20th centuries, which reimagined the medieval fortress as a romantic residence. Giacomo Casanova spent time here in 1773, an episode the castle now leans into as part of its brand identity ("Romance is in our nature"). Lorenzo Da Ponte, the Venetian librettist behind Mozart's "Don Giovanni" and "Le nozze di Figaro," also has documented ties to the estate.

In the 20th century the property was converted into a wine and golf resort, drawing on the terroir of the Collio Goriziano — one of Italy's most sought-after white wine zones. Today Castello di Spessa combines wine production, an 18-hole golf course, and four distinct accommodation areas spread across the estate, keeping the original castle as the symbolic heart and the most exclusive rooms of the complex.

The 19th-century Neo-Gothic restoration that gave Spessa its present silhouette reflects a broader European trend of reimagining older fortresses in a more romantic, castle-like style — meaning the towers and battlements visitors see today are a deliberate 19th-century architectural statement rather than surviving medieval fabric.

The Casanova connection, actively marketed by the estate today, sits alongside the more understated but historically documented link to Lorenzo Da Ponte — together giving Spessa a genuine 18th-century cultural pedigree beyond its architecture.

The estate's four-way split between the castle, La Tavernetta, the hillside Casale, and vineyard apartments reflects a resort that has grown organically around its winemaking and golf operations, rather than converting every historic space into identical guest rooms.

The Collio wine region's international reputation for white wines gives guests staying at Spessa direct access to one of Italy's most respected terroirs, alongside the nearby star-shaped Renaissance fortress town of Palmanova and the historic center of Gorizia.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Castello di Spessa inside the historic castle?
faqs.answer: No — only 15 rooms are within the castle itself. The resort also has La Tavernetta (10 rustic rooms by the restaurant), the hillside Casale (about 10 shabby-chic rooms), and vineyard apartments. Ask specifically for "Castello" rooms if sleeping in the historic building matters to you.

faqs.question: Can I play golf or visit the wine cellars at Castello di Spessa without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes — the 18-hole golf course and the historic wine cellars are open to non-guests, with green fees or a booked tasting.

faqs.question: Did Casanova really stay at Castello di Spessa?
faqs.answer: Yes — Giacomo Casanova spent time at the estate in 1773, an episode the property highlights as part of its identity today.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 35 minutes from Trieste and 90 minutes from Venice by car; the closest airports are Trieste (TRS, ~40 min) or Ljubljana (LJU, ~1h). No nearby train station — a rental car is recommended given the rural, vineyard setting.

**Rooms & rates:** 15 rooms within the castle itself (18th-19th century Venetian style, the most requested); 10 rustic rooms at La Tavernetta by the restaurant; about 10 shabby-chic rooms at the hillside Casale; family apartments among the vineyards. From €189/night. Search specifically for "Castello" rooms if sleeping in the historic building matters to you.

**On-site:** 18-hole golf course, spa, outdoor pool, gourmet restaurant, visitable historic wine cellars, on-site wine tastings.

**Good to know:** A rural area with no public transport — a car is essential. The golf course and cellars welcome outside visitors, so expect some non-guest activity in those areas.

**Combine with:** Gorizia (castle and historic center, ~20 min), the Collio wine region, and Palmanova (a star-shaped Renaissance fortress town, ~40 min).
